Reference / strings/buffer

strings/buffer#

Text built up piece by piece and kept by the runtime: a write does not copy what is already there, and string() gives the text so far.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let page = TextBuffer();
for items -> item {
    page.write("<li>", item, "</li>");
}
page.writeln();
let html = page.string();

Description#

Text built up piece by piece and kept by the runtime: a write does not copy what is already there, and string() gives the text so far.

A TextBuffer is a WritingText, so it goes wherever text is written. Copies of the object share the one buffer, like the other io/buffer views.

Public API#

object TextBuffer#

object TextBuffer does WritingText

Text built piece by piece; a write appends without copying what is there.
